text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and each change triggers automated builds. This means the software is compiled and checked without anyone doing it manually. As part of the process, the team also runs tests automatically. These tests help catch issues early, before they become serious problems. A CI pipeline usually includes building, testing, and sometimes deploying the code. By using CI pipelines, teams can find bugs faster, improve code quality, and work together more efficiently. In short, CI makes development smoother and more reliable.
